A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, equations, figures, and Appendices A–D are readable and support reliable matching across revisions and relocations.

before.justification: V1 reports original simulations on the Random Hierarchy Model and Gaussian random fields, plus forward-backward diffusion experiments on WikiText2 and ImageNet.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and adds empirical comparisons of sampling procedures and classifier-based measurements of the image class transition.

M1.justification: The forward-backward probing method, RHM, diffusion processes, MDLM, and CLIP-based image analysis remain unchanged. Appendix A.1.3 expands the existing BP sampling procedure and evaluates an equivalent sampler without replacing the proposed method.

E1.justification: Both versions use RHM data, Gaussian random fields, WikiText2, and ImageNet. The added sampler and classifier checks examine existing phenomena within this coverage.

E2.justification: V2 Figure 8 newly compares direct BP sampling against backward diffusion using the BP-derived exact score. ConvNeXt in Figure 13 is a measurement instrument, not a competing generative baseline.

E3.justification: The new sampler comparison uses RHM depth L=8 and 32 starting samples. Figure 13 introduces cosine similarity of standardized classifier logits over 10,000 starting images. The settings and sample counts stated for the retained main experiments remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix A.1.3 adds a check that correlation measurements agree across sampling procedures. Appendix D adds classifier-based corroboration of the image class transition. Figure 4 revises two qualitative text examples; the existing Gaussian-field control and critical-scaling analysis remain.

E5.justification: Figure 6 newly reports shaded standard deviations across starting images. Its stated 344 starting images and 128 trajectories per image are unchanged, so this establishes additional uncertainty reporting rather than an increase in runs.

E6.justification: V2 adds sampler-agreement and classifier-logit results in Figures 8 and 13. Figure 6 revises the image curves, including a susceptibility peak of approximately 5.1 versus 5.8 in v1 under the same stated setup. Figure 4 replaces the 0.5 and 0.7 masking examples. The central finite-time peak findings remain.

T1.justification: The labeled definitions and Main result restate existing mathematics. The correlation-length derivation moves from Section 3.1.1 to Appendix A.2.1, retaining its exponent. Equation (28) expresses the existing condition F'(1)<1 explicitly in RHM parameters rather than introducing a new assumption.

C1.justification: The abstract, four introductory contributions, and central conclusions retain the same claims about hierarchical structure, correlated token changes, and finite-noise transitions. Added practical applications are presented as possibilities, not demonstrated contributions.

C2.justification: V2 distinguishes semantic hierarchy from complementary Fourier-scale descriptions and adds possible applications to interpretability and training. It acknowledges that context-dependent language may require more general latent models. Appendix D also newly calls thresholded patch changes statistically significant without specifying a test.

D1.justification: Appendix A.1.3 supplies step-by-step BP sampling details, including production-rule probabilities and message updates. Figure 13 identifies the ConvNeXt Base classifier, its ImageNet-1k pretraining, and logit standardization. These expand documentation without establishing changes to the retained implementations.

R1.justification: V2 adds Rissanen et al. and Wang and Vastola for the semantic-versus-geometrical discussion, Barceló et al. for potential training applications, and Liu et al. for ConvNeXt. Several other references merely receive publication updates.

P1.justification: V2 adds a manuscript roadmap, clarifies diffusion and BP explanations, introduces labeled definitions and a Main result, and relocates the correlation-length derivation to the appendix. It also revises headings and author information while preserving the overall narrative structure.

P2.justification: V2 adds Figures 8 and 13, redesigns Figure 4's text panel, and adds uncertainty bands and revised axes to Figure 6. Retained appendix figures are renumbered, and text examples are redistributed across pages; the overall visual format remains similar.

improvement.justification: The added sampler comparison and classifier-based transition check strengthen the existing evidence, while Figure 6's variability reporting and clearer exposition improve transparency. These gains outweigh localized documentation problems: Figure 4's revised examples no longer match Appendix C, and Appendix D asserts statistical significance without describing a test.
